title: U.S. House · Florida's 9th District
area: Central Florida, including parts of Orange and Osceola counties around Orlando and Kissimmee.

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Darren Soto advanced unopposed. Dan Green won a seven-way Republican primary on August 18, 2026 with 25.4% of the vote, narrowly ahead of Ben Butler (24.4%) and Thomas Chalifoux (20.3%).

candidates.name: Darren Soto

summary.text: Darren Soto is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 9th Congressional District. An attorney from Kissimmee, he served in the Florida House and Senate before his election to Congress in 2016, and now serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

background.text: Born in Ringwood, New Jersey, to a Puerto Rican father and an Italian-American mother; attended Lakeland Regional High School.
Graduated from Rutgers College in 2000 with a B.A. in economics and earned a law degree from George Washington University in 2004.
Moved to Florida in 2002 while in law school and was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2005; practiced commercial, real estate, family and civil rights law.
Worked as president of D. Soto Law Offices and as a financial analyst with Prudential Insurance before entering politics.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives (2007-2012), first elected in a 2007 special election, and in the Florida Senate (2012-2016).
Elected to the U.S. House in 2016; his office describes him as the first congressman of Puerto Rican descent elected to represent Florida.

Assigned to the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where his 2025-2026 subcommittee assignment is Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; has also served on the Natural Resources and Agriculture committees.

According to his official bio, his H.R. 4528 closing a loophole in the Billfish Conservation Act was signed into law on August 2, 2018, and his H.R. 4042 renaming a Kissimmee post office for the Borinqueneers was signed into law on March 23, 2018.

priorities.text: Says he works to help agriculture producers feed America, protect food-assistance programs, combat citrus greening, secure disaster relief, and invest in new agricultural technologies for Central Florida.
Says education is fundamental to upward mobility, and that every child should have access to a high-quality K-12 public education, college or technical education, and lifelong learning opportunities.
Says protecting Florida's environment is a main priority, citing work to restore the Kissimmee River and Chain of Lakes, secure water-supply funding, and protect the Indian River Lagoon.

positions.summary: Says he advocates for renewable energy and tax credits for electric vehicles, hybrid, solar, and wind, and works to protect clean energy.
positions.quote: In the current Congress, he serves on the Energy & Commerce Committee’s Subcommittee on Environment, where he advocates for renewable energy and electric-vehicle, hybrid, solar, and wind tax credits, among other priorities. He also serves on the Natural Resources Committee, where he works to protect clean energy, advance clean water projects, enhance conservation efforts, and more.

positions.summary: His official issues page says he is committed to protecting healthcare and fighting cuts to the Affordable Care Act, Medicare, and Medicaid.
positions.quote: Congressman Soto is committed to protecting healthcare and fighting cuts to the Affordable Care Act (ACA), Medicare, and Medicaid.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 12, the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025 (119th Congress), which would protect access to abortion services.
Cosponsored H.R. 18, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2025 (119th Congress), which would expand background checks on firearm transfers.
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (119th Congress), which would raise the federal minimum wage.
Cosponsored H.R. 7392 (119th Congress), a bill to impose a hiring freeze on U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
In an October 2026 Central Florida Public Media interview he named tariffs among the main drivers of rising costs.
positions.quote: The main drivers of costs right now [are] the tariffs, the war in Iran, and the mass deportations.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; Environment subcommittees) and the Committee on Natural Resources (Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittee) for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Introduced H.R. 9094, the Florida Freeze Disaster Assistance Act of 2026, which would authorize USDA grants to states for agricultural losses caused by freezes.
Introduced H.R. 8728, the Feed Our Kids Act of 2026, which would amend federal child-nutrition law to make school breakfasts and lunches free for all children.

Sponsored the Restoring Resilient Reefs Act, which was enacted as part of the National Defense Authorization Act in the 117th Congress and reauthorizes and modernizes the Coral Reef Conservation Act of 2000.

candidates.researchNotes: Soto has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions, priorities, and sponsored-bill record items above are drawn from his official House issues pages.

summary.text: Dan Green is the Republican nominee for Florida's 9th Congressional District. A Navy Reserve officer who grew up in Indian River County, he served multiple tours in the Middle East and Central Asia and was appointed by President Trump in 2019 as a Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense. His candidate survey lists his priorities as affordability, constitutional government and a strong military.

background.text: Says he grew up in Indian River County, the child of an Army veteran and a school teacher; graduated from Vero Beach High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree from American University (1998), a graduate degree from Florida State University (1999) and a Ph.D. from George Washington University (2012); describes his focus as political science and international relations.
Says he was working in the Pentagon during the September 11, 2001 attacks.

Served in the U.S. Navy Reserve, completing four tours in the Middle East and Central Asia and a civilian tour in southern Afghanistan with the U.S. Department of State; holds the rank of Commander and has been selected for promotion to Captain.
Says he was attached to two SEAL Team deployments, including in Fallujah and southern Afghanistan, and served in Baghdad and Kabul.
Appointed by President Trump in 2019 as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Strategy and Force Development at the U.S. Department of Defense.

priorities.text: "Make America Affordable Again" — lists reducing grocery, gas, and property-insurance costs and balancing the federal budget among his goals.
priorities.quote: Reducing grocery and gas prices, reducing property insurance rates, balancing the budget and paying off the national debt, and having a strong military in order to ensure the peace.

priorities.text: "Restoring Constitutional Government," one of his three named campaign themes.
"Build Peace Through Strength," citing his military and defense-policy background as central to his approach to foreign policy.

statements.quote: While we welcome freedom-loving Americans to our great state, overdevelopment has started to push native Floridians out of their communities.
